data.description:
# Ensure every Main Street card has a dedicated 64×64 sprite

## Problem statement

Every Main Street card renders a square art zone in its top-left corner, but
**108 of the 171 unique cards in `card-data.csv` currently render the same
generic `Fallback` sprite**, so the bulk of the deck is visually
indistinguishable. A player cannot tell an `Upgrade to Patisserie` from a
`Chef` from a `Rainy Day` at a glance, which undermines the 64×64 left-art
redesign's whole purpose.

## Users

- **Player (market / hand / street):** needs to recognise a card by its art
  without reading the title — especially when cards overlap in hand or stack
  on the street.
- **Content author:** needs a documented, testable rule for what art a card
  resolves to, so new cards cannot silently reintroduce `Fallback` art.
- **Engine maintainer:** needs one art-resolution path shared by the runtime
  generator and the static SVG exporter, guarded by a regression test.

User stories:

- As a player, when I look at the market, I can tell any two cards apart by
  their art alone.
- As a content author, when I add a card to `card-data.csv`, the test suite
  tells me if I forgot to give it art.
- As an upgrade card, I show the art of the business I enhance, so my purpose
  is obvious.

## Existing state (verified 2026-09-26, `dev` @ 933644bc)

Resolution path (all four card families call it with the card's `name`):

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCardArt.ts` → `resolveCardArtName()` /
  `hasDedicatedCardArt()`: (1) spelling alias → (2) exact name → (3)
  `Fallback`.
- Map built by `example-games/main-street/scripts/generate-main-street-card-art.mjs`
  from committed `sprites/<Name>_1024_x_1024.png` files into
  `example-games/main-street/card-art-map.json`.
- A second consumer, `example-games/main-street/scripts/generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs`,
  duplicates the alias/lookup logic and must be kept in step (its
  `resolveCardArtDataUri()` reads `aliases` + `fallback` itself).

Verified counts:

- `card-data.csv`: **173 rows / 171 unique names** (the duplicate names
  `Florist` and `Community Garden` appear in two families each — name-keyed
  resolution collides on them).
- Committed sprites: **62 dedicated + `Fallback`** (63 map entries).
- Cards resolving today: **65** (63 exact + 2 via aliases).
- **Cards rendering `Fallback`: 108**, broken down as:

| Family              | Cards | Resolving | Missing |
|---------------------|------:|----------:|--------:|
| business            |    30 |        28 |       2 |
| community-space     |     8 |         1 |       7 |
| upgrade             |    39 |         0 |      39 |
| staff               |    25 |         1 |      24 |
| event               |    71 |        35 |      36 |
| **Total**           |  **173** | **65** | **108** |

> The seed brief's "171 templates / events ~44 / staff 25" figures were
> approximate; the table above is the verified state.

Gap detail:

- **Upgrades (39):** every one carries a populated `targetBusiness`
  (all 39 non-empty; e.g. `Upgrade to Patisserie` → `Bakery`, `Upgrade to
  Adventure Park` → `Playground`). The 39 upgrades map to 31 distinct targets;
  9 of those targets are themselves gaps (`Laundromat`, `Cafe`, `Park`,
  `Library`, `Playground`, `Town Fountain`, `Health Kiosk`, `Community
  Shelter`, `Public Art`). So upgrades can inherit their target's art at zero
  new-asset cost once the target exists.
- **Staff (24 of 25):** no staff art exists at all; `Florist` (staff) only
  resolves because it collides with the `Florist` business name.
- **Events (36 of 71):** includes incidents/opportunities and a block of
  seasonal/cultural cards (`St Patrick's Day`, `Christmas`, `Samhain /
  Halloween`, …).
- **Business (2) / community-space (7):** `Laundromat`, `Cafe`; and all
  community spaces except `Community Garden`.
- Every missing card **already has an `art_notes` description** in
  `card-data.csv` (the same source the existing 1024×1024 sprites were built
  from), but **there is no in-repo image generator** — the 63 sprites were
  committed externally (commit `05026750`). Art creation is therefore an
  out-of-band asset step, not a code step.

## Desired change

Make `hasDedicatedCardArt()` return `true` for all 171 unique cards via a
documented, generated mapping, while keeping `Fallback` as the genuine
last-resort sprite for unknown/future cards.

Recommended (pending producer confirmation — see Open Questions):

1. **Upgrades → target business art.** Resolve `Upgrade to X` to the sprite of
   its `targetBusiness` (explicit override table only where a target has no
   art or the target art is unsuitable).
2. **Events → documented category mapping.** Map each event to a small set of
   category sprites (e.g. by `trigger` — Incident / Investment — combined with
   `targetSynergy`), rather than 36 unique assets.
3. **Staff → dedicated staff sprites** (or a documented small shared set; see
   Open Questions).
4. **Remaining business/community-space gaps (9) → new sprites.**
5. Extend `CARD_ART_ALIASES` (or an equivalent generated mapping) so both
   consumers agree, and keep the generator deterministic.
6. Add a unit drift-guard test over `card-data.csv` asserting AC 1–4.

## Open questions (producer input required)

- **Q1 — Art scope / strategy.** How much new art vs. mapping/reuse for the
  108 cards? **Recommended: reuse-first (Option A)** — upgrades inherit target
  art (0 new); new sprites only for the 9 business/community-space gaps, the
  24 staff roles, and a small documented event category set; events
  category-mapped rather than per-event. Rationale: satisfies the ACs at a
  fraction of a 108-sprite asset effort, while upgrades (the largest family)
  cost nothing.
- **Q2 — Art production ownership & pipeline.** There is no in-repo sprite
  generator; the existing 63 sprites were produced out-of-band. Who produces
  the new 1024×1024 sprites (e.g. agent image generation from `art_notes`,
  commissioned artist), and should this item ship the resolver/map/drift-guard
  machinery first with art as a prerequisite asset item, or wait until the art
  lands? **Recommended:** generate the new sprites from `art_notes` using the
  same out-of-band process as the existing set, committed under this item.
- **Q3 — Event mapping granularity.** If events are category-mapped, what
  taxonomy: by `trigger` (Incident vs Investment), by `targetSynergy`
  (Food / Health / Culture / Commerce / Service / Entertainment), or a single
  shared event sprite? Does the producer accept a category sprite as
  "dedicated" for AC4, or is per-event art required? **Recommended:**
  `trigger` × `targetSynergy` categories (a small, documented set) is
  sufficient for AC4.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Every **unique** card name in `card-data.csv` resolves via
   `MainStreetCardArt.hasDedicatedCardArt()` to a **non-`Fallback`** sprite
   (documented alias/category mapping counts); the current count is 65/171.
2. Upgrade cards resolve to art derived from their `targetBusiness` (or a
   documented explicit override); no upgrade renders `Fallback`.
3. Staff cards each resolve to dedicated staff art (per-role or documented
   shared set); no staff card renders `Fallback`.
4. Event cards each resolve to dedicated or category-mapped art under a
   documented rule; no event card renders `Fallback`.
5. Business and community-space cards all resolve to dedicated art; no card in
   either family renders `Fallback`.
6. A unit-test drift guard over `card-data.csv` asserts AC 1–5 and fails when a
   new card is added without art; `Fallback` remains in the map and resolver for
   genuinely-unknown/future cards (the existing "unknown card" test still passes).
7. Both consumers of `card-art-map.json` (runtime `MainStreetCardArt.ts` and
   `scripts/generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs`) apply the identical mapping;
   regeneration via `scripts/generate-main-street-card-art.mjs` is
   deterministic and reproducible.
8. `docs/main-street/card-dimensions.md` and `public/assets/CREDITS.md`
   document the mapping rules and the licence/attribution of any new art.
9. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
10. `npm run build` is green and the **full project test suite must pass** with
    the new changes.

## Constraints

- New art must be permissively licensed (CC0 / MIT / Apache 2.0) and attributed
  in `public/assets/CREDITS.md`.
- Source art remains `sprites/<Name>_1024_x_1024.png`; `card-art-map.json`
  stays generated (never hand-edited).
- No change to the 64×64 zone geometry, the 140×80 card size, the 256×256
  embedded WebP format, or the SVG being self-contained (inline `data:` URI).
- Mapping logic must be expressed once and consumed by both the runtime and the
  static generator.

## Desired artefacts

- Updated `card-art-map.json` (or equivalent generated mapping) + resolver.
- New `sprites/<Name>_1024_x_1024.png` files per the confirmed strategy.
- Drift-guard unit test in `tests/main-street/`.
- Docs + credits updates.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCardArt.ts` — resolver: add
  targetBusiness/category resolution or extend the alias path.
- `example-games/main-street/card-art-map.json` — regenerated mapping (data).
- `example-games/main-street/scripts/generate-main-street-card-art.mjs` — works
  out the alias/mapping rules from `card-data.csv` + sprites.
- `example-games/main-street/scripts/generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs` —
  second consumer; mirror the mapping.
- `example-games/main-street/sprites/` — new `_1024_x_1024.png` source art.
- `tests/main-street/card-art.test.ts` — add the `card-data.csv` drift guard.
- `docs/main-street/card-dimensions.md` — document mapping rules.
- `public/assets/CREDITS.md` — licence/attribution for new art.

## Risks / assumptions

- **Scope risk (largest):** unique art for 108 cards is a large asset effort;
  the reuse/mapping strategy is the pragmatic first step. Confirmed via Open
  Questions.
- **Art-availability risk:** no in-repo generator exists, so AC 1–5 cannot be
  met by code alone — art is a prerequisite (Open Question Q2).
- **Name-collision risk:** `card-data.csv` has duplicate names across families
  (`Florist`, `Community Garden`); name-keyed resolution assigns both the same
  art. Acceptable, but documented and asserted by the drift guard.
- **Dual-consumer drift risk:** `generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs` duplicates
  the alias logic; a mapping change that misses it silently diverges.
- **Scope-creep risk:** "improve the existing 62 sprites" and "redesign the art
  zone" are out of scope — record as separate work items if they surface.
- **Assumption:** `hasDedicatedCardArt()` remains name-keyed; any targetBusiness
  indirection is baked into the generated map so the public API is unchanged.

## Out of scope

- Changing the 64×64 left-art geometry or the 140×80 card dimensions.
- New card types or `card-data.csv` content changes (beyond `art_notes` if new
  art needs them).
- Redesigning/replacing the existing 62 dedicated sprites.
- Adding an in-repo image-generation tool (unless the producer directs
  otherwise via Q2).

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- Q1 "Art scope / strategy: how much new art vs mapping/reuse for the 108
  cards?" — **OPEN QUESTION** (producer). Recommended: reuse-first (Option A).
- Q2 "Art production ownership & pipeline: who produces the new sprites, and
  does this item ship mapping machinery first?" — **OPEN QUESTION** (producer).
  Recommended: generate from `art_notes` under this item.
- Q3 "Event mapping granularity: what taxonomy, and is a category sprite
  acceptable for AC4?" — **OPEN QUESTION** (producer). Recommended:
  `trigger` × `targetSynergy` categories.

Research summary: verified the resolver, both consumers, the generator, the
test file, and the exact per-family gap counts against `dev` @ 933644bc
(108/171 cards missing art); confirmed all missing cards have `art_notes` and
that no in-repo sprite generator exists (last sprite commit `05026750` was
external).

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **CG-0MP1QZC6Q005EMEZ** – Asset generation: placeholder SVGs for new cards (completed)
- **CG-0MLTFDAYD0J6KLY3** – Phaser Scene Static Card Layout (completed)
- **CG-0MPD5XALT007F1WV** – Gym Graphics: Card Flip Animation (DeckRng + HandPile) (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: 0mtorj5fs006b0un, acceptance, add, alias, apache (+136 more)
- `docs/main-street/prd-milestone-2.md` — matched: acceptance, add, approach, art, asserts (+107 more)
- `AGENTS.md` — matched: acceptance, add, alias, apache, approach (+104 more)
data.title: Assign a dedicated 64×64 sprite to every Main Street card (eliminate generic Fallback art)

## Goal

Fix the shared `HandView` so that, when `maxSlots` is set, card and outline positions derive from the hand's **capacity** rather than the current card count — adding a card never moves an existing card or slot.

## Context

Parent: CG-0MUAYBB4E007LWEQ. Sibling test items add the failing unit and browser tests first.

Root cause: `computeCardPositions()` builds a row centred on `this.cards.length` (`layoutCardPositions({ count: this.cards.length, … })`), and `_computeOutlineSlots()` ghosts it (plus appending extras). The empty-hand branch already lays out the desired fixed `maxSlots` row, so that row is the template to reuse. `getInsertionPosition()`, `rebuildDisplay()`, `applyLayout()`, and the animated `sortCards` path all re-derive the row/rotation normalisation from the occupied positions and must move to the template as well. `setMaxSlots()` currently only rebuilds outlines and does not re-lay the cards.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Parent AC1–AC5: implement the capacity-template behaviour — outline slot positions identical for a hand of 0…`maxSlots` cards; `addCard` fills the next slot right of the occupied run while pre-existing card positions are unchanged; occupied outlines still match card `x/y/rotation` with extras below every card; `setMaxSlots(n)` is the only mutation that re-lays the row and always yields exactly `n` slots; the empty-hand capacity row is unchanged (same centred straight/arc row the cards will occupy).
- Add a shared private helper in `src/ui/HandView.ts` that derives the `maxSlots` template with the existing `layoutCardPositions` maths (gap = `spacing - cardWidth`, `centerX`, `maxWidth` compression, `arcRadius` Y) and the template-span rotation normalisation; recompute from current options on each use (no stale cache).
- `computeCardPositions()` horizontal returns the first `cards.length` template positions; over-capacity cards continue with the template step to the right (best-effort, no re-centring).
- `getInsertionPosition(index)` returns the template position at `index` (first `maxSlots`; template step beyond), so Market→hand transfer animations land exactly on the resting card.
- `_computeOutlineSlots()` derives all `count` slots from the same template (occupied slots ghost the card's **actual** sprite rotation, extras keep `depth = index - 0.5 - count`), replacing the per-count ghosting/extension branch.
- Rotation and arc normalisation in `rebuildDisplay()`, `applyLayout()`, and the animated `sortCards` path use the template span when `maxSlots` is set, so per-card rotation is also stable across adds.
- `setMaxSlots(maxSlots)` re-lays the cards (calls `applyLayout()`), not just the outlines.
- Capacity-driven layout is keyed on `maxSlots !== undefined`, independent of `showPositionOutlines`; toggling outlines never moves cards.
- Hands without `maxSlots` keep the existing centred-on-count layout; vertical cascade keeps `baseY + i * spacing` and is not regressed.
- `src/ui/layoutCardPositions.ts` is reused unchanged.
- The sibling unit and browser test items pass (`npx vitest run --project unit tests/ui/handView.outlines.test.ts`).

**Key Files:**

- `src/ui/HandView.ts` — `computeCardPositions()`, `_computeOutlineSlots()`, `getInsertionPosition()`, `rebuildDisplay()`, `applyLayout()`, `sortCards()` animated path, `setMaxSlots()`.
- `src/ui/layoutCardPositions.ts` — reused to build the capacity row (no change expected).

**Deliverables:**

- Capacity-driven `HandView` layout with stable card and outline slots and green sibling tests.

## Goal

Document the capacity-driven (stable) slot semantics and remove stale wording that describes the hand as centred on the **current** card count (parent AC8).

## Context

Parent: CG-0MUAYBB4E007LWEQ. The fix changes documented behaviour, so the doc-update policy applies: the change and its docs must ship together (or this child blocks parent closure).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Parent AC8: all related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, `docs/DEVELOPER.md` (Hand capacity outlines), `AGENTS.md` if the documented behaviour changes, and any relevant Gym/docs entries.
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` "Hand capacity outlines" states that when `maxSlots` is set the slot row is derived from **capacity**, cards fill it left-to-right, occupied card/slot positions do not move as cards are added, and `setMaxSlots()` is the only operation that re-lays the row; the empty-hand row is unchanged.
- `AGENTS.md` §2 (HandView/PileView key features) hand bullet updated to say slots/outlines are capacity-derived and stable across adds.
- `example-games/gym/scenes/GymHandPileScene.ts` help text describes the fixed-slot behaviour instead of implying per-count centring.
- Stale per-count-centring comments corrected in at least: `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerMarketActions.ts` ("centred on handCenterX" / "left-anchored slot estimate"), `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetRendererStreet.ts` ("centred on handCenterX"), and `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetTutorialHints.ts` (hand-zone comment).
- No player- or developer-facing text still claims the hand is centred on the current card count when `maxSlots` is set.

**Key Files:**

- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — "Hand capacity outlines" section.
- `./AGENTS.md` — §2 hand bullet (and §9 if it repeats the layout claim).
- `example-games/gym/scenes/GymHandPileScene.ts` — help text.

## Intake: producer input required before this item can be scoped

Intake verified the current state against `dev` @ 933644bc and produced a refined brief (now the item description). **108 of 171 unique cards** in `card-data.csv` still resolve to the generic `Fallback` sprite:

| Family | Cards | Missing |
|---|---:|---:|
| upgrade | 39 | 39 |
| staff | 25 | 24 |
| event | 71 | 36 |
| community-space | 8 | 7 |
| business | 30 | 2 |

The code path is clear (one resolver + two map consumers + a drift guard). The blocker is the **art strategy**, which the seed brief explicitly asked the producer to confirm. Three questions (`≤3` per the interview contract):

### Q1 — Art scope / strategy
How much new art vs. mapping/reuse for the 108 cards?
- **Option A (recommended):** reuse-first — upgrades inherit `targetBusiness` art (0 new sprites, covers 39 cards); new sprites only for the 9 business/community-space gaps, the 24 staff roles and a small documented event category set; events category-mapped rather than per-event.
- Option B: unique dedicated art for all 108 cards.
- Option C: pure name/alias mapping onto existing sprites (no new art at all).

**Recommended: Option A** — satisfies the ACs at a fraction of a 108-sprite asset effort, and the largest family (upgrades) costs nothing.

### Q2 — Art production ownership & pipeline
There is **no in-repo sprite generator**; the existing 62 dedicated sprites were committed out-of-band (commit `05026750`). Who produces the new 1024×1024 sprites (agent image generation from `art_notes`, commissioned artist, …), and should this item ship the resolver/map/drift-guard machinery first with art as a prerequisite asset item, or wait until art lands?
- **Recommended:** generate the new sprites from each card's existing `art_notes` using the same out-of-band process as the current set, committed under this item.

### Q3 — Event mapping granularity
If events are category-mapped, what taxonomy: by `trigger` (Incident / Investment), by `targetSynergy` (Food / Health / Culture / Commerce / Service / Entertainment), or a single shared event sprite? Is a category sprite acceptable as "dedicated" for AC4?
- **Recommended:** `trigger` × `targetSynergy` categories (a small documented set) is sufficient for AC4.

**Status:** handing off for producer review; no stage advance. The work item description contains the full brief, mapped rules, AC list, key files and Appendix (Q1–Q3 marked OPEN QUESTION).
